findings.reason: implemented as written, §10 would add two ops that fork an existing owner; correcting the section to name `edit_plan`'s typed-resource path removes the duplicate-implementation instruction the plan currently gives its node.
findings.text: §10's live text still instructs "Add add_milestone/update_milestone", but `edit_plan` already creates and updates milestones through its typed-resource path (resource_type→"milestones" collection at `reckon/mcp.py:1236`; the `set` op's "one top-level field on a sprint/milestone/blocker" help at `reckon/mcp.py:1703`). The plan's own resolved comment concedes the grep searched for op names that were never needed, yet the section text still carries the proposal.

findings.reason: given a validator exists, the authoring templates are a derived artifact and should be generated/validated from the parser/validator rather than hand-copied; the plan's recommendation should route the prompt through `reckon audit-doc` instead of shipping a parallel spelling copy.
findings.text: the §4 copy-paste templates and the §9 "single canonical authoring prompt" are a thin documentation layer over the render contract, and the plan never justifies why the contract in `reckon/_plan_html.py` cannot itself be the documented source — the repo already ships a validator for that contract, `reckon audit-doc` (`reckon/cli.py:8245`) backed by `_audit_document` (`reckon/mcp.py:4757`).

findings.reason: naming `reckon/_plan_html.py` as the owner lets the authoring doc cite and validate against it, whereas the current wording invites drift and the silent section loss the plan's comment thread already records.
findings.text: §4 makes the plan its own normative spelling source ("Reuse the exact class/attr names from §4"), but the owner of those names is `_RENDERERS` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1160`) and `_SECTION_RECOGNISED_SPELLING` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:1270`), from which `parse_plan`/`write_state` derive. A second normative copy in the plan is exactly the divergence the plan's own evidence documents (`article.r-decision[data-id]` parsing empty against the canonical `div.r-dec[data-key]`).

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan proposes no new code module; §9 reduces the machine-readable surface rather than adding a wrapper set over it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan makes its own §3/§4 the normative statement of the machine-readable contract, which duplicates the spelling/rendering owner in `reckon/_plan_html.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §10's live text proposes `add_milestone`/`update_milestone` MCP ops that duplicate `edit_plan`'s existing typed-resource milestone path (`reckon/mcp.py`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — the §4 templates and §9 "canonical authoring prompt" are a thin hand-copied documentation layer over the render contract owned by `reckon/_plan_html.py`, with no statement of why that contract cannot be the single documented source.
